structure.heading: Accountable Ownership and Milestone Roadmap to Close Remaining Savings Gaps (May–Dec 2026)
text_content: **Accountable Ownership and Milestone Roadmap to Close Remaining Savings Gaps (May–Dec 2026)**

Accountability for delivery of the cost transformation programme is vested at executive level: Sarah Patel (CFO) is the Accountable Executive Owner with full programme authority for decisions, prioritisation, and sign-off. Operational accountability for a material portion of the remaining gap sits with Mark Lewis (VP Procurement), who is expressly accountable for £9.0m of the outstanding £13.3m. A clear RACI has been established: Sarah approves strategy and escalations; Mark owns supplier negotiations, category plans, and procurement execution; business unit leads own implementation. All accountable owners are required to attest monthly to progress, variances, and mitigating actions. Performance expectations include adherence to the milestone roadmap and achievement of specified cost reductions within agreed timelines and quality constraints. Standards.

The milestone roadmap closes the remaining £13.3m gap by 31 Dec 2026 through three delivery checkpoints: 30 Jun 2026, 30 Sep 2026, and 31 Dec 2026. Targets are staged to de-risk execution: deliver £4.0m by 30 Jun 2026, reach a cumulative £9.0m by 30 Sep 2026 (this tranche is the primary focus of Mark Lewis and the Procurement function), and finalise the remaining £4.3m by 31 Dec 2026. Key initiatives tied to each checkpoint include supplier re-negotiations, demand-management levers, and category consolidation. Responsibility for individual initiatives is allocated to named owners in the initiative register, with Procurement, Finance, and Operations each accountable for measurable deliverables and acceptance criteria at each milestone. Change control gates will govern scope.

Monitoring, reporting, and risk mitigation standards will ensure closure to plan. A weekly operating cadence (consolidated into a monthly executive pack) will report realized savings, run-rate impact, forecast attainment versus the £13.3m target, and variance explanations. KPIs include month-on-month cashable savings, contract renegotiation win-rate, and delivery velocity against each milestone; thresholds are defined so that a >5% shortfall versus plan at any milestone triggers an immediate remedial action plan and escalation to Sarah Patel. The next governance checkpoint is the Steering Committee on 15 Jun 2026, at which owners will present RAG-rated progress, validated savings, and a revised risk-adjusted forecast to support final decisioning and resource reallocation through to 31 Dec 2026 and contingency.

structure.heading: Programme Savings Position and Gap-to-Target (FY2025 YTD)
text_content: As of 30 Apr 2026, the programme has identified £48.5m of gross annualised savings opportunities. As of 30 Apr 2026, £21.7m of annualised savings has been realised and validated by Finance. The FY2026 target is £35.0m annualised savings, leaving a £13.3m gap as of 30 Apr 2026. On a percentage basis, realised savings represent 62.0% of the FY2026 target and 44.7% of the total identified opportunity; the identified opportunity equates to 138.6% of the FY2026 target. These figures establish the starting position for FY2026 year-to-date performance measurement and prioritisation.

The composition of the £21.7m realised savings is concentrated across operational levers: Procurement initiatives account for £9.2m, Workforce optimisation £6.0m, IT rationalisation £3.1m, Estates and property consolidation £1.4m, and Process improvement and automation £2.0m. All realised savings have been validated by the Finance control team and reflected in the month‑end ledger as of 30 Apr 2026, enabling accurate forecast updates. These line‑by‑line values inform variance analysis against business unit budgets and support Directorate-level reporting to the CFO and Programme Board. The mix confirms procurement remains the largest contributor to validated outcomes YTD.

The outstanding £13.3m gap as of 30 Apr 2026 comprises a mix of committed and contingent opportunities: £8.0m of initiatives are contractually or operationally committed and expected to convert with high probability, while £5.3m sits in the contingent pipeline requiring approvals or supplier negotiation. If only the committed £8.0m converts, FY2026 attainment would reach £29.7m (21.7+8.0), or 84.9% of the £35.0m target; full conversion of the £5.3m contingent pipeline would close the gap to achieve 100.0% attainment. Key risks include timing slippage and governance delays; mitigations are prioritised approvals, accelerated procurement engagement, and monthly Finance gating to secure validation and oversight.
